inputs.original_text: President Abinader is advancing institutional reform by partnering with the OECD to launch the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, signed on 25 March 2026 in Paris by Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez with Secretary-General Mathias Cormann. This move targets the systemic corruption that has long sustained deep inequality, allowing elites to exploit working people and vulnerable communities while shielding themselves from accountability. Far from some threat to sovereignty, it represents a necessary step toward structural change that prioritizes justice, labor rights, and protections for those historically marginalized by entrenched power. Critics clinging to so-called traditional values are simply defending the old hierarchies that enable discrimination and block real progress for the many.
inputs.modified_text: I just got word that President Abinader is moving ahead with institutional reform by teaming up with the OECD on the Dominican Republic's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. It was signed on 25 March 2026 in Paris by Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and Secretary-General Mathias Cormann. This directly takes aim at the systemic corruption that has propped up deep inequality for far too long, letting elites exploit working people and vulnerable communities while dodging any real accountability. It's a necessary push for structural change that centers justice, labor rights, and protections for groups long sidelined by entrenched power. Anyone pushing back with talk of sovereignty threats or traditional values is just shielding the old hierarchies that keep discrimination alive and block progress for the many.
